summary.short: Amends Virginia Code § 32.1-127 so that hospitals, nursing homes and certified nursing facilities must establish and implement policies on patient access to and use of intelligent personal assistants during inpatient services, with health information protected under HIPAA. Approved March 18, 2021.
summary.long: Chapter 219 (2021) amends and reenacts § 32.1-127 of the Code of Virginia, which governs regulations of the Board for hospitals, nursing homes and certified nursing facilities. The AI-relevant addition is a subdivision requiring each hospital, nursing home and certified nursing facility to establish and implement policies ensuring the permissible access to and use of an intelligent personal assistant provided by a patient, in accordance with the Board's regulations, while the patient receives inpatient services. These policies must ensure protection of health information under the federal Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996. The subdivision defines an intelligent personal assistant as a combination of an electronic device and a specialized software application that assists users with basic tasks using natural language processing and artificial intelligence, including digital or virtual assistants. The provision states no penalty of its own; the other subdivisions of § 32.1-127 concern hospital and nursing-home standards and are outside the scope of this annotation. The document as provided does not mark which text is newly added, so the annotation rests on the intelligent personal assistant subdivision only.},

notes: This is the session law (Chapter 219, Acts of 2021, approved March 18, 2021) that reenacts Code § 32.1-127 in full. The text does not mark added or changed language, so the new intelligent personal assistant subdivision in subsection B cannot be separated from restated text here; check the official session law. Every item in subsection B is numbered 1. in the source, so provision references describe items by subject. The bill number HB 2154 appears only in registry metadata, not in the document. The intelligent personal assistant duty refers to 'such regulations' without naming them.

thresholds.variable_text: minimum liability insurance coverage amount for nursing homes and certified nursing facilities
thresholds.measurement: liability insurance coverage maintained by the facility; measurement method not specified
thresholds.consequence: Failure to maintain such minimum insurance shall result in revocation of the facility's license.
thresholds.conditions: Applies to each nursing home and certified nursing facility; separate professional liability coverage must be at least equal to the recovery limit in § 8.01-581.15.

evidence.quote: maintain liability insurance coverage in a minimum amount of $1 million

thresholds.variable_text: duration of exemption from the license requirement for adding temporary beds
thresholds.value_text: for a period of no more than 30 days
thresholds.measurement: period of the exemption, running from the Commissioner's determination
thresholds.consequence: The exemption from the license requirement to add temporary beds lasts no more than 30 days.
thresholds.conditions: The Commissioner has determined that a natural or man-made disaster has caused the evacuation of a hospital or nursing home and that a public health emergency exists due to a shortage of hospital or nursing home beds.

evidence.quote: for a period of no more than 30 days

thresholds.variable_text: anticipated or actual length of stay of a potential patient for sex offender registry ascertainment
thresholds.value_text: a length of stay greater than three days or in fact stays longer than three days
thresholds.measurement: anticipated length of stay at admission, or actual length of stay if it exceeds three days
thresholds.consequence: The nursing home or certified nursing facility must ascertain, prior to admission, whether the potential patient is required to register with the Sex Offender and Crimes Against Minors Registry.
thresholds.conditions: Applies to nursing homes and certified nursing facilities; the ascertainment duty concerns patients who are required to register under Chapter 9 of Title 9.1.

evidence.quote: a length of stay greater than three days or in fact stays longer than three days
